summary: Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa from circa 1845 to 1865.

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna. He served there as a professor from 1797 to circa 1831 and later became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca, later becoming a professor at Sapienza in 1932 and president of ISMEO from 1947 to 1978.

Giuseppe Vignato specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, holding an attested post there in 2017.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Sylvain Lévi, Taiken Kimura, and others. He worked as an assistant at the University of Tokyo in 1926 and became a professor at Toyo University in 1927.

Glenn H. Mullin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Tenzin Gyatso. In 1984, he founded The Mystical Arts of Tibet.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Godabarish Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy after studying at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya, served as headmaster at Chakradharpur High School, and was a director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, later serving as a lecturer in Mongolian at Far Eastern Federal University from circa 1906 to 1917.

Gopinath Kaviraj worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis and held multiple posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including librarian, principal (1923–1937), and head of the Yoga-Tantra Department (1964–1969).

Gordon D. Kaufman was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned degrees from Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. He held positions at Pomona College and Vanderbilt University before becoming Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard in 1963.

Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Cambridge and served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from circa 1920 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson is an historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as President of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1993–2010), Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cambridge (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).
Gottfried August Bürger studied at the University of Göttingen from 1768 to 1772. He later held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1789 until 1794.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen and served at Vilnius University from circa 1804 to 1824.

Gottfried Hermann was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena. He served at Leipzig University as an extraordinary professor of philosophy in 1798 and as director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

Gottfried Kinkel was an historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn from 1831 to 1834. He held academic posts at the University of Bonn (circa 1836–1849) and ETH Zurich (circa 1866–1882).

Gotthilf Heinrich von Schubert was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena. He held academic posts at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from circa 1819 to 1827 and the University of Munich from circa 1827 to 1853.

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and history who studied at the University of Königsberg. He held posts at the University of Königsberg and Königsberg Cathedral before becoming a professor at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1726–1737).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London and Heidelberg University. He taught at King's College London, served as Principal of Government College University, Lahore, and became the first Registrar of the University of the Punjab.
